text:
A: Hiya! Oh my god, finally, I'm Holly. Okay, confession straight away: I told Gemma last round I'd already had you, and I hadn't, I'd got you muddled with someone. So hello, properly this time!
B: Ha! Hiya, I'm Ceri. No, Gemma did mention a Holly. I thought, who's this then, telling stories about me already?
A: Only nice ones, I promise! Wait, hang on, we've got the same hair. Is that weird? We've literally got the same hair.
B: I clocked that in your photo! Copper twins. Mine's out of a box, mind, and I used to do it for a living, so that's shameful.
A: You was a hairdresser? Oh, you have to tell me, because my roots are horrendous. Be honest.
B: Honest? Erm, you're about two inches overdue, lovely. And you've gone a shade too warm at the ends, it's started going a bit pinky. A gloss would sort that, it's not a disaster.
A: Pinky! Oh no. Tom said nothing, the traitor. Tom's my husband. Sorry, where are you, actually?
B: Pontypridd. Valleys. And I'm doing OT at Cardiff now, mature student, so the hair's for mates in my kitchen these days. For cash, don't tell anyone.
A: Your secret's safe. I'm a PhD student in Birmingham, geography. Derelict warehouses, canals, that sort of thing. I basically climb through fences and call it research.
B: Oh, I love that. Do you do the urban exploring stuff? Dai, my partner, watches them videos on YouTube, people in old asylums.
A: Yes! Exactly that, but with ethics forms. I did an old pumping station last month, pigeons everywhere, my film camera jammed, and I sort of fell through a floorboard. Well, my leg did. Okay, my foot.
B: It's getting smaller as you tell it!
A: Ha, it was a big foot in my head. Do you go to gigs? You look like a gig person.
B: Oh, all the time. Little venues in Cardiff, Welsh bands mostly, indie stuff. Saw a lush one last month in a room above a pub, about forty people, sweating like anything.
A: That's my favourite kind. I was in Digbeth last weekend and someone poured a pint down my back. I told the girl before you, Lauren, and she said that's exactly why she doesn't go to gigs.
B: Aw, Lauren! I had her last round, she's a sweetheart. Told me my dog's lump is probably just fat. Cheaper than the vet.
A: She's lovely, isn't she. Kind of shy, but then she gets going about anaesthetic and she's brilliant. Okay, bread roll. Go.
B: Ha! I've been asked this already. It's a roll. Or a bap. But I'm saying barm now, Gemma's converted me, I said it to Dai last night and he looked at me like I'd had a stroke. Sorry, that's a bit dark, my dad actually had one.
A: Oh no, I'm sorry. Is he alright?
B: He's doing tidy. It's why I went into OT, really. Watching them get him back making his own cuppa. Anyway, what's your Pickle like? I saw a grey tail.
A: Diva. Won't go out in the rain, won't eat cold food. I love her to bits. Do you do charity shops? Because I got a seventies suede jacket for eight quid the other week and I need someone to appreciate it.
B: Eight quid! Where? Ponty's charity shops are all Primark cast-offs now. I had a proper rummage in
